title: Infrastructure as Code (OpenTofu & Terraform)
summary: Provision reproducible cloud and Kubernetes infrastructure using OpenTofu and Terraform: HCL modules, remote state locking, plan/apply workflows, and drift detection.
learningObjectives: Execute the full OpenTofu/Terraform lifecycle (`init`, `validate`, `plan`, `apply`, `state list`).
Provision cloud VPC, EKS cluster, and S3 state infrastructure declaratively.
Audit and reconcile infrastructure state drift.

curriculumModules.title: Declarative HCL, State Graphs & Provider Plugins
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: OpenTofu (CNCF / Linux Foundation open-source Terraform fork) builds a dependency DAG of infrastructure resources, compares HCL against remote state, and executes API calls in topological order.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Store encrypted state remotely (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) with state locking enabled and client-side state encryption (`encryption` block in OpenTofu).

curriculumModules.title: Reusable Modules, Drift Detection & Policy-as-Code
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Versioned modules encapsulate VPC, Kubernetes, and IAM patterns while `tofu state list` and `tofu plan -detailed-exitcode` detect out-of-band console drift.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Run `tofu plan` on every Pull Request and gate `tofu apply` behind automated OPA/Conftest policy checks.

labs.title: Provisioning Cloud-Native Infrastructure with OpenTofu
labs.scenario: Initialize and apply an OpenTofu configuration (`tofu init` and `tofu apply`) to provision the production VPC and EKS cluster resources.
labs.productionContext: All production cloud environments must be provisioned through version-controlled OpenTofu/Terraform workflows rather than manual ClickOps.
objectives: Apply the infrastructure plan using `tofu apply` to provision `aws_eks_cluster.prod`

steps.title: Initialize OpenTofu Workspace
steps.instruction: Run `tofu init` to initialize providers and state backend.

steps.title: Apply Declarative Infrastructure Plan
steps.instruction: Run `tofu apply` to provision the VPC, EKS cluster, and S3 artifact bucket.

validationRules.description: Cloud resource aws_eks_cluster.prod provisioned via tofu apply
validationRules.name: aws_eks_cluster.prod
validationRules.remediation: Run `tofu apply` to provision cloud resources.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Run `tofu init` followed by `tofu apply`, then inspect with `tofu state list`.

labs.title: Auditing Terraform State & Deploying Workload ConfigMap
labs.scenario: Audit managed infrastructure in the state file using `tofu state list` and publish the cluster endpoint into ConfigMap `production/terraform-outputs`.
labs.productionContext: Bridging IaC outputs into Kubernetes ConfigMaps allows workloads and GitOps controllers to consume cloud resource identifiers cleanly.
objectives: List tracked resources in OpenTofu state using `tofu state list`
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1

steps.title: Inspect OpenTofu State Graph
steps.instruction: Run `tofu state list` to audit resources tracked in the state file.

validationRules.description: Audited state via tofu state list

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure `tofu state list` was executed and `ConfigMap/terraform-outputs` exists in `production`.

assessmentQuestions.question: Why is remote state locking (e.g., S3 + DynamoDB or native S3 lockfile) critical when multiple engineers or CI jobs run OpenTofu/Terraform?
options: It prevents concurrent `apply` runs from corrupting the state file or creating conflicting duplicate cloud resources
assessmentQuestions.explanation: State locking ensures only one process can mutate the infrastructure state graph at a time, preventing race conditions and state corruption.

assessmentQuestions.question: Which OpenTofu command validates the syntax and internal consistency of `.tf` files without accessing remote cloud APIs?
assessmentQuestions.explanation: `tofu validate` checks HCL syntax, attribute types, and module references locally without requiring cloud credentials or network calls.
